- The prior triage note (2026-11-05, task 10217) recorded findings but produced no decision record, which is why the doctrine re-queued it. Its content is still correct and is not contradicted by anything landed since.

## What this issue actually owes

A recorded design decision for the **adapter conformance harness** (the test suite every transport adapter must pass) and the **interop matrix run in CI** ("adapters are certified, not hoped"). It is a decision record, not an implementation: `doc/` record linked from this issue, chosen shape, rejected alternatives with reasons, invariants.

## Ordering and dependencies (verified fresh)

- Parent: **#5674** (wire format & transport adapters) — OPEN.
- Siblings under #5674: #5808 (postcard wire schema v1), #5809 (versioning/negotiation/forward-compat), #5810 (framing & fragmentation per carrier), #5811–#5813 (the adapters themselves), #5815 (security binding review). All OPEN.
- #5975 (closed, PR #7602) makes this issue **load-bearing**: its interop contract names the wire format, identity, capability negotiation and registry format as the load-bearing elements, and explicitly assigns "conformance proof" to #5814. So this design is the proof obligation for the self-hosting/interop stance, not an optional extra.
- Consequence for sequencing: the harness can be designed now against the contract shape (certification criteria, matrix axes, CI gate placement, fixture/oracle model), but the **matrix cells and assertion set must be filled from #5808/#5809/#5810/#5811–#5813 as they land**. The record must therefore either pin the contract versions it was written against or state that cell population follows the siblings — the same shape used by the #5866 decision record (decided half + explicitly blocked remainder with a resume condition).

## Repo state relevant to the design (checked)

- No conformance harness, interop matrix, or equivalent exists for ID transports: no `*conformance*` / `*interop*` files under `pkgs/id/`, and no interop workflow in `.github/workflows/`.
- `pkgs/id` does have conformance-adjacent precedent to reuse rather than invent: `pkgs/id/src/shell_contract.rs` + `shell_contract/tests.rs` and `pkgs/id/src/world_session/contract_tests.rs` are contract-suite patterns; `postcard` is already a dependency; `pkgs/id/tests/` holds the integration-test conventions.

body:
The ID program review found one concrete mapping the harness still needs. [#5811 §3.3 and §7 invariant 9](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/3caf6f23de9913bd115c47035a856be955f5b4f1/doc/2026-11-08T09-45-00Z_design_id5811_wss_https_adapter.md#L157) says HTTPS POST reassembly refuses reordered chunks and defers to #5810. [#5810 §3 rules 4–5](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/3caf6f23de9913bd115c47035a856be955f5b4f1/doc/2026-11-09_decision_id5810_carrier_framing.md#L72) explicitly separates datagram/store-and-forward arrival from canonical validation order. The stream carrier's ordering guarantee has a different scope. The records leave the mapping of a frame split over multiple HTTPS POSTs ambiguous.

For the harness, classify that HTTPS path first. Then specify the expected outcome for two valid chunks arriving in reverse order, an exact duplicate, conflicting bytes under the same chunk identity, and an incomplete assembly. Assert the reconstructed bytes or explicit refusal and the absence of partial frame delivery. Preserve per-request stream order and session gap handling. This records a narrow open decision on the existing harness tracker. It does not claim that an implementation violates either profile. [Program #13240](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13240).

Lane code-j: decision record for this design is in PR #13734 (`doc/decisions/ID-5814-adapter-conformance-and-interop.md`). Settles harness shape, oracles, generated interop matrix (smoke in merge gate, full nightly), and invariants I1-I5. Open points recorded with defaults. Design only, nothing built. Issue stays open for the first implementation slice (harness trait + golden-vector runner) when it is scheduled.

Second-pass verify-and-route (oc-code-07, task 21851), state checked 2026-11-24.

The design is settled in substance. The recorded decision is on main as doc/decisions/ID-5814-adapter-conformance-and-interop.md (merged via #13734 on 2026-11-24), building on the earlier design record #7853 (merged 2026-11-14). The ticket asked for a recorded decision with the shape, the rejected alternatives and the invariants, and that is what the record contains. No PR is open for this issue and no implementation follow-on is required now; implementation timing is a separate decision, as the body notes. Closing as resolved by the decision record.
